A share is a piece of a company: you get a slice of its profit and its problems, and what it is worth moves with what buyers will pay that day. One share in one company can halve; a fund holding hundreds of companies spreads that risk, which is why most people should start with an index fund inside an ISA.

In England and Wales you apply to the family court yourself, online, and you do not need a solicitor to do it: the application says the marriage has broken down and, since April 2022, why is not asked. It costs £593, you can ask the court to make your ex pay half, and there is a discount if you are on a low income. Nothing happens quickly - 20 weeks after the application you can apply for the conditional order, then six weeks and a day later for the final order, so about seven months at the shortest. Deal with the money and the house in a separate financial order, because the divorce itself divides nothing, and get that agreed before the final order, not after. Scotland goes through the sheriff court and has a cheaper simplified divorce if there are no children under 16 and little to share.

Ask work first, then price the journey three ways before you buy anything: a season ticket only beats weekly or daily tickets above about three days a week, a flexi ticket or a carnet covers two or three days, and a railcard pays for itself in about a dozen trips if you qualify for one. If you drive, park and ride, a lift-share board or a parking space a ten-minute walk out usually undercuts the station car park, and asking whether your employer does a season ticket loan or a cycle-to-work scheme is free money in effect. Booking the next day's travel the night before is where the cheap fares go.

Work in per 100g, not per serving, because serving sizes are chosen to look small.
